The T+1 open is 19:00-05:15 in all of them, so this is NOT a third clock-time transition — but it IS a third place where the editions disagree, and it is exactly the product-existence defect the Taiwan boundary note refuses to commit ("reporting those contracts open through 2020 asserts a product that the cited edition does not contain"). The two families are treated asymmetrically on identical evidence.

INTERSECTION WINDOW — the stated start 2020-01-01 cannot be affirmed for Taiwan. The claim as given to me says the served intersection for 2020-01-01..2025-04-06 includes `Taiwan 14:15`; under the 2020 extracted state taiwan_t1 is UNKNOWN, so the window is not "true under EVERY extracted state in that interval" — it is true only from the 2021-01 edition forward. (The code itself does not make this error: Taiwan's first revision is 2021-01-01, and the sgx_equity_index_more.rs note qualifies it as "Taiwan T+1 14:15 (from the 2021 edition; see the boundary note below)". The defect is in the claim as summarized, not in the served data.) For the other five families the intersection is arithmetically exact and I confirm it: Japan pre-2025 state is 07:30-14:25 ∪ 14:55-05:15 and the 2025-01 state is 07:30-14:55 ∪ 15:25-05:15; their set intersection is 07:30-14:25 ∪ 15:25-05:15, precisely as claimed — 14:25-14:55 is excluded (closed in the old state) and 14:55-15:25 is excluded (closed in the new state). China 17:00, SiMSCI 17:50 and NTR 19:00 are constant across every edition in the interval, so their intersection is trivially themselves.

EXTRACTION-QUALITY CAVEAT — edition 2022-06 is a visual read, not a text extraction. Its own caveat: pdftotext -layout "produced only 152 bytes of garbage glyphs", the text is converted to vector outlines (single embedded font GloberBold, no ToUnicode map), and the values were read off pdftoppm renders at 200-300 DPI; the extractor states "if your pipeline requires reachable to mean specifically 'pdftotext yielded text', treat this row as reachable=false". All six of its values match both neighbouring editions exactly, so the risk to the 'no third transition' conclusion is low, but one of the eight rows underwriting the agreement claim is not machine-verified.

COVERAGE GAP — the 2025-11 edition is not in the extracted evidence. sgx_equity_index.rs claims "NINE PUBLISHED FILES ... of which eight are distinct documents" and asserts "2025-11/DT Trading Calendar 2025.pdf is byte-identical to 2025-07/DT Trading Calendar 2025 (updated 31 Jul 2025).pdf". The evidence set has exactly eight rows and none for 2025-11, so that byte-identity assertion is unverified here. Impact is nil for the disputed window: 2025-11 falls entirely after the 2025-04-07 cutover and could not change the 2020..2025-04-06 intersection.
result.reasoning:
METHOD: I compared all six fields across all eight extracted rows, then checked every field the claim does NOT tabulate (session starts, T-session ends, T+1 ends) for a hidden third transition, then verified the intersection arithmetic as a set operation, then read the actual Rust source to distinguish an error in the served data from an error in the claim's summary.

NO THIRD CLOCK-TIME TRANSITION EXISTS. Every untabulated bound is constant across all eight editions: Japan T start 07:30 (2020 through 2026-01), China T 09:00-16:30 (unchanged even in 2025-07 and 2026-01: \"9:00am to 4:30pm 4:45pm to 5:15am\"), SiMSCI T 08:30-17:20, Taiwan T 08:45-13:45 wherever known, NTR T 07:25-18:30, and T+1 end 05:15 in every family in every edition. The two tabulated transitions verify exactly: 2024→2025-01 moves japan_t 07:30-14:25→07:30-14:55 and japan_t1 14:55→15:25 with all four other families unchanged; 2025-01→2025-07 moves japan_t1 15:25→15:10, china 17:00→16:45, simsci 17:50→17:35, taiwan 14:15→14:00, ntr 19:00→18:45 with japan_t unchanged at 07:30-14:55 (consistent with the circular's \"no change to the T session trading hours\"). 2026-01 is identical to 2025-07 on all six fields.

WHY I STILL ANSWERED false ON ALL THREE FLAGS. (1) table_matches: the 2020 row's Taiwan cell is UNKNOWN in evidence, so the printed table asserts a value it cannot source. (2) exactly_two_transitions: the editions disagree in a third place — product coverage. Edition 2020 has no FTSE Taiwan suite at all, and the NTR (USD) suite's membership changes twice (FN* absent in 2020; MCN* absent through 2022-06; NSG absent in both 2021 editions). \"Exactly two places\" is true of the clock times and false of the editions taken whole. (3) intersection_correct: literally read, the question asks whether the window is true under EVERY extracted state in the interval, and under the 2020 state Taiwan is UNKNOWN.

IMPORTANT QUALIFICATION, so this is not read as worse than it is: the Taiwan defect is confined to the summarized table. The code already gets Taiwan right — SGX_EQUITY_INDEX_TAIWAN_REVISIONS starts 2021-01-01, the boundary note reproduces the evidence's reasoning almost verbatim (including that TWN is a holiday-market code in 2020 and that the identical MSCI predecessor hours are not a licence to start a year earlier), and the intersection note qualifies Taiwan as \"from the 2021 edition\". The one finding that is NOT already handled, and the strongest item here, is the NTR asymmetry: the same argument the code makes for Taiwan applies to FN* before 2021-01 and MCN* before 2024, and the NTR profile nonetheless starts 2020-01-01 covering them.
